name: Der Dihedral
approach: Approach as for Backbone Ridge and Serpentine Arete: from the Stuart Lake Trailhead (3,400 ft) follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 to the signed junction at 2.6 miles, then Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.3-4.4 miles, ~2,200 ft gain, 2-2.5 hours). From the lake, follow the lateral moraine/talus below Dragontail's north face as for Backbone Ridge, but Der Dihedral's start is lower on the face and a couple of ridgelines short of (east/right of, and below) Backbone Ridge proper - it is not as well-cairned or as heavily travelled as the Backbone/Serpentine approach. Look for a clean left-facing dihedral a pitch or two up the initial ridge; because the route sees little traffic, budget extra time for route-finding to the exact start from the moraine (scanning from lake level with binoculars helps). Total approach roughly 3-3.5 hours from the trailhead.

itinerary.cal: Requires a Colchuck Lake overnight permit (May 15-Oct 31 lottery) if camping; the route is drier/less traveled than Backbone Ridge proper, so expect more route-finding on the lower pitches.

days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake Trail to Colchuck Lake and camp below the north face, the shared base for this and the neighboring Backbone Ridge.
days.title: Approach to Colchuck Lake camp

days.note: Pre-dawn approach to a start a couple of ridges below the standard Backbone base, climb a clean dihedral a couple of pitches up, then join the Backbone Ridge for its finish to the summit (6 pitches total). Descend via Aasgard Pass back to camp.
days.title: Climb Der Dihedral into Backbone Ridge, descend to camp

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Dihedral pitches low on the formation.

schedule.label: Join Backbone Ridge
schedule.detail: Merge with the standard ridge line.

days.objective: Summit via Der Dihedral and the Backbone finish

days.note: Break camp and hike back out to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-3 day trip: camp at Colchuck Lake, then a full alpine day (10-12 hrs) climbing the dihedral into the Backbone Ridge finish and descending to camp before hiking out.
